Then replace full boards end to end rather than patching a section — a butt joint mid-span will cup and catch feet. Use coated deck screws long enough to bite the joist by an inch and a half.
Should I pull all the boards in that run while I'm at it, or just the three?
Just the three, unless the neighbors are cupped too. New boards next to weathered ones will look different for a season, so set them with the same gap, about an eighth inch, and let them grey out.
Separate question — the bathroom fan upstairs runs but nothing comes out, and the mirror fogs up in about two minutes.
That's usually a disconnected or crushed duct, or a fan moving too few CFM for the room. Go up and check where the duct actually goes before replacing the fan.
I looked — it just dumps into the attic a foot above the insulation.
That's the problem. It's pushing warm moist air straight into the attic, which is why the mirror fogs and why you may get frost or mold on the roof sheathing. It has to vent outdoors.
The roof is a 4/12 pitch. Can I go out the gable end instead of cutting the roof?

Yes, gable end is easier and much less likely to leak. Use insulated flex or rigid duct, keep the run short and sloping slightly down toward the outside, and put a proper louvered hood with a damper on the wall.

title: Deck boards and an attic fan

messages.text: I want to tile the kitchen backsplash myself. The wall behind the counter is 11 feet long and 20 inches tall, but the range hood cuts out about 30 inches wide by 20 tall.
So roughly 220 inches of wall minus 600 square inches for the hood, about 12.5 square feet. Buy 15 square feet of tile for cuts and breakage.
Should I use mastic or thinset? It's painted drywall back there.
Mastic is fine over painted drywall in a dry area, and it's easier for a first job. Scuff the paint with 80-grit first so it grabs. Thinset only if it's near the sink and gets splashed a lot.
ok. how much grout do I need for that area?
One 10-pound bag of unsanded grout covers about 30 square feet with 1/8-inch joints, so a single bag is plenty, with some left over for touch-ups.
What about the outlets? Do I cut around them or pull them out?
Kill the breaker, pull the outlets out of the boxes, and tile over the box with a cut that leaves the screws clear. Then add an extension ring so the outlet sits flush with the new tile face.
yes, do that. what order do I go in?

Start at the counter and work up, set the full tiles first, then cut the top row and the hood edges last. Let it cure overnight before grouting, and caulk the bottom joint at the counter instead of grouting it.
Last thing, do I need to sand the whole wall or just where the mastic goes?
Just the areas you'll cover, but go a couple of inches past the tile line so nothing squeezes out onto smooth paint. Wipe the dust off with a damp rag and let it dry before you start.
One of the torsion springs on my garage door snapped last night. A company quoted $480 to replace both springs and lubricate the door. Is that reasonable?

That's in the normal range for a two-spring replacement with a service call, though the springs themselves are only $60 to $100 for the pair. You're mostly paying for the labor and the risk of winding them.
The door is a single 8-foot-wide wood door, fairly heavy. Does the spring size change the price?
A little. Heavier doors use thicker wire, which costs more, but not $200 more. Ask what spring they're putting in — you want the cycle rating, something in the 15,000 to 25,000 range.
and the other one? There's a second quote coming tomorrow.
Compare on the same terms: both springs, new center bearing plate if yours is worn, and a warranty on the springs. If the second quote is within $50, take the one with the longer warranty.
Should I just do it myself? I've watched videos.

I'd say no. Winding torsion springs takes two proper winding bars and a lot of force, and a slip can break a wrist. If you want to do part of it, lube the rollers and hinges and let them handle the springs.
Fair enough. What should I ask them before they start?
Ask whether they'll check the door balance and the cable condition while they're in there, and get the spring cycle rating and warranty in writing on the invoice.
I'm replacing the treads on my basement stairs. Thirteen steps, 36 inches wide, and the stringers are sound. What thickness of oak should I use?
One-inch oak treads are standard for 36-inch widths at a 10-inch depth. If there's any flex in the stringers, go to 1-1/16 or add a center support.
And the risers, should I keep the old pine ones or replace them?
Replace them while the treads are off — they're cheap and you'll never get a clean paint line against new finish otherwise. Three-quarter plywood or 1x8 pine, cut to each rise.
The nosings overhang about an inch. Any problem with that?
Up to 1-1/4 inch is fine and normal. Just keep every nosing the same so the overhang doesn't vary by a quarter inch from step to step.
Ok, now the handrail. Code is 34 to 38 inches above the nosing, right?
Yes, measured vertically from the nosing to the top of the rail, and it has to be continuous along the whole run. Keep it consistent pitch with the stairs rather than levelling it.
Do I need a rail on both sides? The right side is a wall, the left is open to the room.
The open side needs a guard and a rail; the wall side is optional. Since your stair is only 36 inches wide, one rail on the open side meets the requirement.
So put it on the open side. What brackets work on a 2x4 wall stud?
Lag the brackets into studs, not the drywall, 2-1/2 inch lags at least. If the studs don't land where you need them, add a 1x4 backing board screwed across three studs and mount the brackets to that.

title: New stair treads, then the handrail

messages.text: My attic has about 4 inches of old blown-in fiberglass. I want to get to R-49. How many bags of the loose cellulose from the box store do I need for 900 square feet?

Cellulose runs about 3.5 per inch, so R-49 needs roughly 14 inches total. With 4 inches already there, you'd add about 10 inches, which is around 30 bags for 900 square feet at the coverage on the bag.
Does depth matter if the joists are only 2x6? Won't it bury the tops?
It will, and that's fine — blow right over the joists. Just mark the depth with a ruler stapled to a joist every few bays so you can check as you go.
What about the soffit vents? Do I need baffles everywhere or just at the eaves?
At every bay that has a soffit vent, and keep the insulation a couple inches clear of the roof deck there. Without baffles you'll block the intake and the attic will run wet.
Separate question, nothing to do with the house: my daughter's science fair project is mold growth on bread. What's a good way to set it up?

Use four or five slices from the same loaf, seal each in its own labeled zipper bag, and vary one thing: light versus dark, or dry versus a few drops of water. Check them at the same time each day and photograph from the same angle.
How do we keep the results from just being mold everywhere by day three?
Use the fridge for one sample and room temperature for another, and keep the added water to a few drops rather than soaking the bread. That slows the fast ones and gives you a spread to measure.
Ok. One thing on the project: how long does it take before there's anything to see?
Usually three to five days for the first spots, and a week to ten days to get clear differences. Start it on a Friday so the weekend checks are easy.

task: Attic insulation and a school project
title: Attic insulation, then a science fair

messages.text: I need to send the monthly invoice to the café on Bridge Street, and I think last month's was wrong.
What did you put on last month's?
Eleven trays of croissants at £24 and forty loaves at £3.10. They say they were billed for twelve trays.
Then they're right and you owe them £24 back. Raise a credit note for one tray against the original invoice number rather than editing it.
Ok. How do I word the credit note?
Something like: Credit note CN-041, against invoice 118, one tray of croissants billed in error, £24.00. Then a line saying it'll be deducted from the next invoice.
Same for the loaves? They only queried the trays.
No, forty loaves at £3.10 is £124 and that matches the delivery sheet, so leave it alone.
Right. And when should this month's go out?
Their terms are 30 days from invoice date, so send it the last Friday of the month like you have been. That keeps the payment landing before your own flour bill.
I'll do it Friday then, with the credit note attached.

title: Invoice for the Bridge Street café

messages.text: My accountant wants my mileage for the tax return and all I've got is a shoebox of fuel receipts.
Do you have any record of journeys, or only the receipts?
Just receipts. About £2,300 of diesel since April.
You can either claim the actual running costs or use simplified expenses at a flat rate per business mile. The flat rate is usually simpler to defend.
The van's in my own name, not a company van.
That's fine, simplified expenses are for sole traders using their own vehicle. It's 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles, then 25p after that.
I did about 14,000 miles this year, but maybe 3,000 of those were personal.
Then only the 11,000 business miles count. 10,000 at 45p is £4,500, plus 1,000 at 25p is £250, so £4,750.
That's better than the receipts. Can I just use that figure?
Yes, but once you use simplified expenses for the van you should keep using it for that van in later years.
Fine, I'll use it. Do I still need to keep the fuel receipts?
Not for the mileage claim itself, but keep a note of your business miles per trip or per week, and hold on to the receipts anyway for six years.
I'll start a notebook from Monday and back-fill what I can from the diary.
That'll do. Send the accountant the £4,750 figure and a line saying it's simplified expenses for 11,000 business miles.
Antalis invoiced us for twenty reams of 120gsm uncoated but only sixteen came off the pallet and two of those were water-damaged.
Have you told them yet?
Yes, they said raise a credit request and quote the order number.
Then put the PO number, the delivery date, and the driver's name if it's on the paperwork. Photograph the damaged reams before you bin them.
The order number is PO-4471, delivered Thursday.
Write it as: PO-4471, 20 reams 120gsm uncoated ordered, 14 usable on arrival, 2 water-damaged, 4 short. Please credit six reams at the invoiced rate.
Do I credit the whole invoice or just the six reams?
Just the six. Pay the rest as normal so you don't upset the account terms, and note the credit on the remittance.
Got it. Separate thing — for the Hollis brochure job, can I run 170gsm through the duplexer?
Depends on the machine. What's its rated maximum weight for duplex?
It's the Xerox 550, the spec sheet says up to 220gsm.
Then 170gsm is fine both sides. Just set it to heavy paper so it slows the fuser down, or you'll get curl on the second pass.
And the 300gsm for the cover would have to go on the litho?
Yes, 300gsm is past what that feeder will take reliably. Run the covers litho and leave them a day before folding.
Mrs Aldridge rang about the front border we did on Tuesday. She says we cut back her peonies.
Does the job sheet mention them?
Job sheet just says tidy front border, cut back shrubs to 30cm. Nothing about the plants at the edge.
Then it's arguable but she's still a customer. Offer to come and look before you offer money.
She wants £60 off the £340 invoice.
That's reasonable for a lost season's flowers. Give her the £60 and keep the job — she's got three neighbours who use you.
I'll do that. Should I put anything in writing?
A short note on the revised invoice: goodwill reduction of £60 agreed for plants cut in the front border, balance £280. That's enough.
Different topic — my van's MOT is up on the 14th and the brake warning light came on this morning.
Get the light looked at before the test, not after. A steady brake light is often just low fluid, but it can be a seized caliper.
The garage can't fit me in till the 20th. Can I keep driving it?
No. Once the 14th passes you can't drive it on the road at all except straight to a pre-booked test, and a brake warning makes it worse.
So I need to find someone before the 14th.
Yes, ring round for an MOT slot this week and get the light checked at the same time. Keep the booking confirmation in the cab in case you're stopped.
